summary: Not an allocated object: the generated class is the packed-pixel plane read by Video_FilterPackedBytesWord4 (0x0013E924) - 0x100-byte rows of 4-byte packed samples. The 'fields' are only the words that filter touches, in rows 0, 1, 2 and 4.
evidence: Body of 0x0013E924/0x00144F24: `uVar2 = 0x7F7F7F7F & *arg1 >> 1`, then `arg1[0x40]`, `arg1[0x80]`, `arg1[0x100]` are the same five words one row further, and the loop does `arg1 += 0x80; arg2 += 0x80` (two 0x100-byte rows per pass). So byte 0x100 is one row and the recorded offsets are plane samples, not members of a struct.

fields.evidence: `f3c0 = self->f_3c0;` is the stored Y motion-vector predictor: `f3c0 >> 1` indexes luma rows (`*0x100` pitch), `f3c0 >> 2` chroma rows, and `f3c0 & 1` selects the filter phase row; ReadMv accumulates the delta into it, ApplyMv reuses it.

summary: Not an allocated object: one view of the shared motion-compensation context (McCtx) used by Video_McPredict3ApplyMv4 (0x0013B120, 0x00141720). Holds the 0x100-pitch frame-plane pointers at +0x0C/+0x24 and the accumulated motion-vector predictor at +0x3BC/+0x3C0.
evidence: 0x0013B120, 0x00141720: `iVar2 = self->f_3bc; f3c0 = self->f_3c0;` then three indirect subpel calls: luma arg1 `*(int*)(self + r5 + 0xc) + ...`, arg2 `self->f_c + ...`; two chroma calls use `*(int*)(self + r5 + 0x24)`. Variant 3: luma subpel table 0x5A5C, chroma 0x5CEC; block emission 4/4 (wrappers pass r5=0x10 offset, r6=0x02 size). No ctor/vtable: a McCtx slice, not its own class.

fields.name: lumaFramePlane
fields.evidence: Arg1 of the subpel filter is `*(int*)(self + blockOffset + 0xc) + x + (mvY>>1)*0x100 + (mvX>>1)` and arg2 is `self->f_c + x`, so +0x0C holds the first of the luma frame-plane pointers (blockOffset 0x04/0x08/0x0C/0x10/0x14 from the tiny wrappers selects another 0x100-pitch plane). Type left void* because only pointer arithmetic is visible.

fields.name: chromaFramePlane
fields.evidence: Both chroma filter calls address `*(int*)(self + blockOffset + 0x24) + (x>>1) + (mvY>>2)*0x100 + (mvX>>2)`, the second 0x80 (0x100 in the _C half-size copy) further for the other component, so +0x24 holds the first of the chroma frame-plane pointers, mirroring the luma array at +0x0C.
